description: The computed report of an autario data app on the caller's own connected data (Google Search Console, GA4, Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, Meta Ads, Google Ads, Shopify, ChatGPT and other assistants), or a public bubble check on a stock.

app.description: Which operation to run. audience_360 = audience, acquisition and conversion across web and social (sign-in); seo_360 = Search Console actions: gaps, decay, cannibalization (sign-in); content_360 = which pages and posts perform (sign-in); social_360 = followers, reach, engagement and posts per channel (sign-in); marketing_report = spend, revenue and ROAS per channel for a brand (sign-in); ai_visibility_360 = how AI assistants mention your brand (sign-in); projects = your project board, grouped (sign-in); project = one project with milestones and KPIs (sign-in); project_objectives = objectives and key results with derived status (sign-in); bubble_or_not = public valuation check on a stock ticker, needs ticker.

brand.description: audience_360: The brand (connector grouping) id to report on, as a uuid. Omitted means the brand selected in the autario app (the account's stored brand choice), so you see what the user sees on screen; with no brand selected, all of the account's brands. A non-uuid value is read as `brand_term` instead, so a caller written before 2026-09-22 keeps working. seo_360, content_360, social_360: The brand (connector grouping) id to report on, as a uuid. Omitted means the brand selected in the autario app (the account's stored brand choice), so you see what the user sees on screen; with no brand selected, all of the account's brands. A brand that is not yours answers an error, never another brand's numbers. marketing_report: The brand id (uuid) to report on. Omitted means the brand selected in the autario app (the account's stored brand choice); with none selected, the account's Default brand, which is where every unassigned connector already belongs. Every response lists the caller's brands, so a first call without this argument tells you what to pass next. ai_visibility_360: Brand name or brand id. Optional when the account has exactly one brand; with several brands the tool answers with the list so you can re-call with one (nothing is picked for you).

brand_term.description: Optional brand TERM override for the brand-vs-generic query split (default: derived from the GSC property). Renamed from `brand` on 2026-09-22, when that word became the connector grouping everywhere; a non-uuid `brand` is still read as this.

channel.description: Optional single-channel filter (sections that cannot honor it say so in notes).

chart_type.description: Optional render style for the fundamental: line or bar. Default is the app's smart choice (bars for quarterly reports, line for daily-derived metrics).

client.description: Deprecated spelling of `brand`, still accepted so callers written before 2026-09-22 keep working. Pass `brand`.

countries.description: Optional comma-separated ISO country codes filter, e.g. "DEU,USA".

days.description: seo_360: Analysis window in days (7-90, default 28), anchored at the newest day of the caller's data. The trend comparison uses the same-length window before it. content_360: Analysis window in days (7, 28 or 90, default 28), anchored at the newest day of the caller's Search Console data and folded into ISO weeks. The change compares against the same-length window before it. social_360: Analysis window in days (7-90, default 28). Each platform anchors it at the newest day of ITS OWN connector table, because connectors refresh on different rhythms. ai_visibility_360: Analysis window in days over the stored runs (1-365). Omit it for every run the brand has (the default).

format.description: Output wire format for this MCP call. Default 'toon' (Token-Oriented Notation, fewest tokens, best for tabular rows). 'compact' = minified JSON. 'json' = pretty JSON for readability. The REST API always returns JSON regardless.

from.description: audience_360: Custom window start (YYYY-MM-DD), only with range=custom. marketing_report: Start day (YYYY-MM-DD) when period is "custom". An unusable pair falls back to the default window rather than erroring.

group.description: For "list": which axis the cards are folded on. Default "okr", which is the axis that answers "does everything we do pay into something we agreed".

id.description: The id of the thing to read or change: the project for "get" and "update", the objective for "update_objective", the key result for "update_key_result".

instances.description: Optional comma-separated connector instance ids, to narrow the report to some of the connections inside the selected brand (for example one of two Search Console properties). Omitted means all of them. An id that is not yours, or not in that brand, answers an error rather than a quietly shorter report. The ids are the instance ids my_workspace action "app_context" returns for this app.

metric.description: Optional fundamental to overlay against price. One of the labels from the company's available metrics (e.g. "Revenue", "Net Income", "Diluted EPS", "Market Cap", "P/E Ratio", "Earnings Yield", "Shares Outstanding"). If omitted, a sensible default is chosen. The response lists available_metrics so you can re-call with another.

period.description: The reporting window. Default last-30. "this-week" runs Monday to today and compares to the same weekdays one week earlier; "custom" needs `from` and `to`.

range.description: audience_360: Time window preset. Relative presets anchor at the newest data day. Default 90d. Use "custom" together with from/to. bubble_or_not: Optional time window for the chart. Default ALL (full history).

scale.description: Optional value scale. "absolute" = raw values on a dual axis. "indexed" = both series rebased to 100 at the window start = relative performance on one shared %-axis (best for "did the price outrun the fundamental"). Default absolute.

sections.description: audience_360: Which report sections to return. Default ["overview","channels"]. Request only what the question needs (token efficiency); call again for more. seo_360: Which report sections to return. Default ["page2_gaps","health"]. Request only what the question needs (token efficiency); call again for more. content_360: Which report sections to return. Default ["overview"]. Request only what the question needs; call again for more. social_360: Which report sections to return. Default ["score","health"]. Request only what the question needs (token efficiency); call again for more. activity = the activity table: every post with platform, content type, topic, post type, sentiment and language, per-dimension pivots and the (platform, content type, topic, language) groups that beat the platform median; labels come from the user's own classification run. marketing_report: Which report sections to return. Default ["overview"]. Request only what the question needs (token efficiency); call again for more. ai_visibility_360: Which report sections to return. Default ["overview"]. Request only what the question needs (token efficiency); call again for more. searches = the web searches the assistants ran behind their answers (grouped by topic, brands named in them); movers = cited domains that are new / trending / losing against the prior window; pages = the cited pages with what is ON them (title, page type, which tracked brands the page names); crawlability = what each domain's robots.txt says to each AI crawler (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot...) plus llms.txt; perception = the descriptor words the answers use next to each brand, as a brand-by-word matrix; action_effects = the brand's visibility 14 days before and after every action marked done; gaps = the sources that cite a competitor and never this brand, with gap score, used-as-a-source share, prompt coverage and competitor rate (each defined on the page; there is deliberately no retrieval rate, because only citations are observable); model_rankings = the brands each assistant names most, as a rank order with the owned brand flagged.

sort.description: social_360: How the cross-platform top-post list is ranked (posts section). Default engagement. The three rates rank only posts whose platform reports them (Instagram today). projects: For "list": the order of cards inside each group. "board" (default) puts off-track work first; "effort_impact" orders by impact (5 to 1) then effort (fewest days first), unrated work last. No combined score is computed.

ticker.description: US stock ticker symbol, e.g. AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, TSLA, AMZN

to.description: audience_360: Custom window end (YYYY-MM-DD), only with range=custom. marketing_report: End day (YYYY-MM-DD) when period is "custom".

name: app_report
